source.title: Shinners & Mahler's Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas
source.authors: Diggs, G. M. Jr.; Lipscomb, B. L.; O'Kennon, R. J.

morphology_documented.bark: Mottled orange-to-salmon patches and thin flaking bark (genus key)
morphology_documented.leaves: Leaves 20–60 mm, usually once serrate, nearly symmetrical at base, smooth above
morphology_documented.fruit: Hairless roundish or round-ovate samara ca. 10 mm long

source_scope_note: Direct species-level details separated from genus/key information; absent historical treatments not filled by unsupported inference.
unresolved_taxonomy_or_source_notes: Chinese lacebark elm introduced from China and Japan, not locally native
Distinguish from Ulmus pumila: spring flowering and no conspicuous orange-salmon mottling for U. pumila
preservation: Additive record only; photos, credits, species records and published site unchanged
